advisor.hypothesis: The scenario screens near_wake and far_wake as 0.0 configured coverage: the blockMesh background (h=0.588 m) and the level-4/5 distance shells stop at ~0.11 m from the surface, so the entire downstream corridor is unallocated. Adding two graded flow_refine boxes that exactly reproduce the requirement envelopes raises coverage to ~1.0 while keeping each corridor solidly inside the 4x-per-decade refinement ceiling above level 2. The dominant cost is the boundary-layer stack (855k of the 2.29M forecast) because 8 layers of 1.2948 mm on ~36 m2 is a large footprint on a 12M budget; I therefore coarsen the far wake to level 2 rather than 3 to fund the near-wake level 4 while leaving unresolved_feature_fraction unchanged.
advisor.expected_change: Near-wake cell axis span ~0.0367 m (level 4), i.e. ~5.2x below the 0.1893 m gate; far-wake ~0.147 m (level 2), ~2.6x below the 0.3787 m gate. Configured coverage 0.0 -> 1.0 for both requirements; scenario_screen.accepted 0.0-state false -> true. Forecast total 2.29M -> 2.45M, ~20% of the 12M ceiling, background and near totals unchanged; initial_certification stays ok with unresolved_feature_fraction 0.0984. Uncertainty: the count is an unvalidated conservative geometry estimate, not a measured count, and cell-axis span is not a verified shear-layer resolution - no shear thickness has been measured.
alternatives: near level 4 / far level 2 (selected): coverage 1.0, total 2.45M, near/far margins 5.2x / 2.6x
near level 3 / far level 2 (previewed): total 2.45M but only 2.6x near-wake margin, weaker rear-separation and shear-layer support
near level 4 / far level 3 (previewed): total 3.50M, 43% more cells for far-wake resolution that steady RANS does not need
no flow_refine at all: forecast 2.29M but both requirements stay at 0.0 coverage and the scenario screen remains unaccepted
counterevidence: Wake location, separation and vortex trajectory are unvalidated_physical_hypothesis, so these boxes are planning envelopes, not measured flow; the scenario itself states off-body resolution is screening only.
Deeper near-wake refinement cannot be justified: no shear-layer thickness or vortex-core radius has been measured, so no cells-across-shear count can be claimed.
Max_refinement/level-6/7 feature boxes already dominate the unresolved-feature accounting, so lift in the wake does not reduce feature_fraction and these boxes are not a geometry repair.
The free-air boundary environment excludes ground, moving belt and wheel rotation, so any apparent wake or force improvement must not be read as physical validation.
level 4 for near wake carries an error if actual shear layers are thinner than the planning prior; that must be settled by a later flow sensitivity, not by adding more boxes now.

advisor.hypothesis: Both rounds share one root mechanism, not a wake-allocation problem: the layer stack is being destroyed by the shrinker/thickness machinery interacting with warped snapped surface polygons, producing 5 highly-skew faces (max_skew 4.68 vs limit 4.0), invalid native boundary polygons, a 0.218 area fraction with ZERO actual layers, and only 33.8% area with >=5 layers. The repair_0 local_refine at level 6 (field-sampled, not medial-distance based) landed on the same warped polygon cluster (skewFaces:16) and instead INCREASED skew from 4.68 to 5.75 while leaving coverage flat (0.3334 -> 0.3379) — so more surface refinement is not the mechanism; the extrude/shrink step itself is over-driving cells near the snapped cluster. The realistic, certifiable intervention is to (a) disable medial-axis displacement over-drive by relaxing the thickness-to-medial clamp and the extrusion angle gate so layers shrink instead of inverting on warped faces, (b) cheaply re-snap with a tighter tolerance and more feature-snap iterations to remove the few warped faces that break native planar-kernel observation, and (c) reduce the outer layer count so the outer slices stop competing for the same thin fluid gap.
advisor.expected_change: max_skew from 4.68 toward <4.0 and the 5 highly-skew faces removed; invalid/warped native boundary polygons reduced so native boundary observation becomes available; area fraction with 0 actual layers from 0.218 toward <0.10 and >=5-layer area from 0.338 toward >=0.60. Layer coverage is expected to be partial, not certified 0.90. Cell count stays near 1.86M (<2M), so extra budget is available if this direction is confirmed. Uncertainty: the torus counterexample shows shrinker changes alone can be ineffective on some geometry; if skew and coverage remain flat, the extruded layer mechanism is not recoverable within the 12M/quality budget and the case should be reported as uncertified rather than patched with more boxes.
alternatives: Keep 8 layers but switch mesh_shrinker to displacementMotionSolver with Laplacian/inverse-distance diffusivity to smooth the shrinking near the warped cluster — deferred because motion solver alone gave 1.74% coverage in the torus counterexample and cannot be tested for free.

Increase n_surface_layers to 10-12 to buy outer layers after shrinking: rejected because it adds stack thickness on the same thin fluid gaps that already produced 0.218 zero-layer area, worsening the failure rather than curing it.

Raise global surface_level to 6 (surface_refine) to better resolve the 0.0026-0.0117 m feature tail: rejected because round-1 already showed local refinement at the same cluster increases skew (native shows 1.86M cells at level 5 with skew 4.68; level 6 raises cell count ~8x locally and cannot relax the 4.0 skewness gate).

Add a level-3 flow_refine jacket around near_wake to blend the level-4/2 interface: rejected because native near_wake p95 span is 0.0431 m and far_wake 0.1511 m, already 4.4x and 2.5x inside their 0.189/0.379 m gates, so wake resolution is not the binding constraint.
counterevidence: Round 0 and round 1 are single/dual-action probes with identical layer parameters (8 layers, first 1.2948 mm, ratio 1.2, max_thickness_to_medial_ratio 0.3, min_medial_axis_angle 90), so their similar 0.333/0.338 coverage is consistent with the layer step — but causation is not proven because no probe varied the shrinker alone.
feature_angle is already 60 deg (strict); raising it further suppresses extrusion and would widen the 0.218 zero-layer area — hence I loosen it rather than tighten it.
n_grow would zero displacement on neighbours and, per the v2412 reference, trades coverage for safer transitions; coverage is already the failing metric, so it is left at 0.

The measured first_height p50 1.2948 mm and inferred y+ p50 50.0 sit inside the 30..300 wall-function window; only the p5 (25.2) tails out, so the failure is warp/shape of a minority of faces, not a uniform first-height mis-calibration — therefore no wall_height change without a sane measured field.

actions.why: Target the actual skew mechanism: on warped snapped faces the medial-axis mover drives displacement until the thickness/medial-direction test trips, bending cells. Reducing n_surface_layers 8->6 preserves the required >=5 actual layers while removing the two outer slices that compete for the thin gaps, and dropping expansion_ratio 1.2->1.15 keeps the stack 0.0067 m — well under the 0.0701 m boundary-layer estimate — so the first height (1.2948 mm, y+ p50 50) is untouched and remains inside 30..300. n_buffer_cells_no_extrude 0->1 holds one no-extrude buffer on the warped cluster so the transition has room instead of forcing extrusion into a corner; n_layer_iter and n_smooth_thickness are raised to smooth the shorter stack before final quality checks. n_grow stays 0 because it propagates non-extrusion and would further cut already-insufficient coverage.

The native boundary polygon is too warped for planar-kernel observation, which also blocks the layer-coverage audit. Tightening tolerance 2.0->1.2 and explicit_feature_snap true->false keeps the waviness at the snapped cluster (skewFaces:16 / concaveFaces:8 region) from projecting faces onto sub-grid slabs, while n_feature_snap_iter 10->18 and n_relax_iter 7->12 smooth the residual warp. This targets native polygon validity and the max_skew gate together; it does not add cells or change the wake envelope.

advisor.hypothesis: The binding failure has changed and is no longer the round-0/1 story of skew-driven layer destruction. Round 2 removed the skew failure (max_skew 2.95 vs limit 4.0; checkMesh reports n_failed 0), yet layer coverage FELL from 0.338 to 0.178 and the zero-layer area fraction rose to 0.245. The native mechanism log is explicit: geometry coverage 73.2% (105461/144006 faces), 'Reducing layer thickness at 18947 nodes where thickness to medial axis distance is large', 'Removing isolated regions ... exclusively surrounded by non-extruded faces', and a second pass extruding 105452/144006 (73.2%) — i.e. the stack is limited by extrusion opportunity, not by count. The query resolves the cause into two distinct mechanisms rather than one: (A) at layer_shortfall:0 (body_area 1.477 m2) the native retained thickness-truncation diagnostic shows wall-to-medial distances p50 0.0163 / p95 0.0229 m and area_fraction_by_layers 0 = 0.403 — the 19k 'reduced thickness' nodes ARE this cluster, so the 6-layer stack was allowed to extrude but then clamped by max_thickness_to_medial_ratio 0.45 against the NATIVE FLUID medial distance. Round 2 actually RAISED that ratio 0.3->0.45 and also raised min_medial_axis_angle 90->70, which permits steeper extrusion directions and therefore MORE over-thick halving — consistent with coverage halving. This is a layer-shrinker clamp failure, not underresolution and not a corner/feature_angle failure (fraction of adjacent edges above the 70 deg feature angle is only 0.091 at :0 and 0.035 at :1).
